title: Grade 5 Science — Wed, Jun 03
description: The Skeletal System — Day 3 of 5: Muscles and movement
subject: science

questions.question: Bones cannot move on their own. They are moved by:
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on the bones to move them; bones cannot move by themselves.

questions.question: Muscles are attached to bones by tough cords called:
questions.explanation: Tendons are strong cords that attach muscles to bones.

questions.question: A muscle moves a bone by:
options: Pulling it as the muscle shortens
questions.explanation: When a muscle contracts (shortens), it pulls the bone and moves it.

questions.question: Muscles usually work in:
questions.explanation: Muscles work in pairs — one pulls the bone one way, the other pulls it back.

questions.question: When you bend your arm, the muscle on the front (biceps):
questions.explanation: The biceps contracts to bend the arm, pulling the lower arm bone upward.

questions.question: When one muscle of a pair contracts, the other one:
questions.explanation: In a muscle pair, when one contracts the other relaxes, so the bone can move smoothly.

questions.question: The muscle of the heart works:
options: All the time without us thinking
questions.explanation: The heart muscle works on its own, all the time, without us having to think about it.

questions.question: Muscles that we move when we want, like arm muscles, are called:
questions.explanation: Voluntary muscles, like those in the arms and legs, move when we choose to move them.

questions.question: Which activity helps to keep our muscles strong and healthy?
questions.explanation: Regular exercise keeps muscles strong, fit and healthy.

questions.question: Why does the body need both bones and muscles to move?
options: Bones bend and muscles are stiff
Muscles pull and bones provide the firm parts to move
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones, and bones act as the firm levers that actually move.

questions.question: The muscle at the back of the upper arm (triceps) helps to:
questions.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten the arm, working as the partner of the biceps.

questions.question: Tendons differ from ligaments because tendons join:
questions.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone, while ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.question: Muscles that work without our control, like those in the stomach, are called:
questions.explanation: Involuntary muscles, like the stomach muscles, work on their own without our control.

questions.question: When you walk, your leg muscles and leg bones work together at the:
questions.explanation: Walking uses leg muscles pulling bones at the knee and hip joints.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about muscles?
options: They can only push, not pull
They pull bones to create movement
questions.explanation: Muscles move the body by pulling on bones when they contract.
